claims.claim: AT&T's structural path is fiber plus wireless convergence: dense access infrastructure connects households and enterprises to recurring communications needs, while copper retirement can shift capital and customers toward higher-capability networks.

The bottleneck is not exclusive: cable, fixed wireless and other fiber networks can substitute, so resilience depends on convergence economics, footprint quality and disciplined capital deployment rather than access ownership alone.

causalEdges: fiber access + wireless network -> converged connectivity -> household/enterprise communications
copper retirement -> lower legacy burden + migration -> advanced connectivity mix
capital intensity -> required cash generation -> network expansion resilience

risks.risk: Capital intensity and credible access substitutes constrain bottleneck power; legacy runoff must be replaced economically.

contradictions.contradiction: Advanced connectivity growth coexists with deliberate legacy contraction, so consolidated growth can obscure replacement economics.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental ROIC and retention economics of the expanded/acquired fiber footprint remain unknown.

claims.claim: The convergence thesis remains plausible but is not proven by subscriber or revenue growth alone; it requires evidence that lifetime value, churn and incremental returns offset discounts, acquisition costs and network capital intensity.
Buybacks alongside expected higher leverage are not inherently contradictory, but they increase dependence on durable free cash flow and disciplined transaction integration.

causalEdges: convergence discounts -> retention benefit only if lifetime value exceeds ARPU concession
buybacks + higher leverage -> capital allocation pressure -> dependence on FCF durability

risks.risk: Leverage, fiber integration, capital intensity and legacy contraction can reduce flexibility if free cash flow weakens.

contradictions.contradiction: Capital returns are accelerating while leverage is expected to rise; sustainability depends on free-cash-flow durability.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run converged-customer lifetime value and acquired-fiber ROIC are not established in current evidence.
